mcqs.question: Which of the following statements best defines the inertia of motion?

options.A: A tendency of a moving object to continue moving with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
options.B: A tendency of an object at rest to stay at rest unless a force is applied.
options.C: A tendency of a body to resist any change in its shape.
options.D: A tendency of a moving object to speed up spontaneously.

mcqs.answer: A tendency of a moving object to continue moving with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion refers to the resistance of a moving body to any change in its state of uniform straight‑line motion. Option A captures this definition. Option B describes inertia of rest, C is about rigidity, and D is incorrect because objects do not accelerate without a force.

mcqs.question: A passenger feels thrown outward when a car suddenly takes a sharp turn. Which aspect of inertia explains this sensation?
mcqs.explanation: When the car changes direction, the passenger’s body tends to continue moving in the original straight line. This resistance to a change in direction is called inertia of direction. Option A refers to speed, C to stationary objects, and D is not a distinct type of inertia.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly states Newton's first law of motion?

options.A: An object will accelerate if a net force acts on it.
options.B: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
options.C: An object remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.
options.D: The force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration.

mcqs.answer: An object remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.
mcqs.explanation: Newton's first law (law of inertia) states that a body will maintain its state of rest or uniform straight‑line motion unless a net external force changes that state. Option A describes the second law, B the third law, and D is the mathematical form of the second law.

mcqs.question: Which everyday situation best illustrates the inertia of direction?

options.A: A ball rolling on a frictionless surface continues to move forward.
options.B: A car continues straight ahead when the driver turns the steering wheel sharply.
options.C: A book remains motionless on a table until pushed.
options.D: A skydiver slows down after opening the parachute.

mcqs.answer: A car continues straight ahead when the driver turns the steering wheel sharply.
mcqs.explanation: The car’s tendency to keep moving in its original straight line despite the steering input demonstrates inertia of direction. Option A shows inertia of motion, C shows inertia of rest, and D involves air resistance, not inertia of direction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about inertia is correct?

options.A: Inertia is the force required to start the motion of a stationary object.
options.B: Inertia is the property of matter that resists any change in its state of motion.
options.C: Inertia is the tendency of a moving object to speed up on its own.
options.D: Inertia is the same as weight.

mcqs.answer: Inertia is the property of matter that resists any change in its state of motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is an inherent property of mass that opposes changes in speed or direction. Option A confuses inertia with force, C incorrectly suggests spontaneous acceleration, and D confuses inertia with weight (gravitational force).

mcqs.question: A stationary ball placed on a perfectly horizontal, frictionless surface remains at rest. Which principle best explains this observation?
mcqs.explanation: Because no net external horizontal force acts, the ball’s tendency to stay at rest—its inertia of rest—keeps it stationary. Newton's second law relates force to acceleration, which is zero here; gravity acts vertically; momentum conservation is not the primary explanation for a body initially at rest.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares inertia of motion with inertia of direction?

options.A: Inertia of motion resists changes in speed, whereas inertia of direction resists changes in the direction of motion.
options.B: Inertia of motion resists changes in direction, whereas inertia of direction resists changes in speed.
options.C: Both terms describe the same resistance to any change in motion and are interchangeable.
options.D: Inertia of motion applies only to objects at rest, while inertia of direction applies only to moving objects.

mcqs.answer: Inertia of motion resists changes in speed, whereas inertia of direction resists changes in the direction of motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion (or of speed) refers to the resistance to a change in the magnitude of velocity, while inertia of direction refers to resistance to a change in the line of motion. Options B, C, and D misstate these definitions.

mcqs.question: A spacecraft coasting in deep space far from any gravitational fields moves with a constant velocity. According to Newton's first law, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The spacecraft will eventually stop because of its inertia of motion.
options.B: The spacecraft will continue to move with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force.
options.C: The spacecraft will gradually change direction due to its inertia of direction.
options.D: The spacecraft will accelerate spontaneously because of its inertia of rest.

mcqs.answer: The spacecraft will continue to move with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force.
mcqs.explanation: Newton's first law states that in the absence of a net external force, a body maintains its state of uniform straight‑line motion. Hence the spacecraft will keep moving unchanged. Option A incorrectly suggests it will stop, C misinterprets inertia of direction, and D mixes concepts incorrectly.
